content:
ajay: FYI seeing a cluster of scheduling failures for GPU pods in us-west1-b starting ~10:10 UTC. Pods are Pending with `No nodes are available` even though total regional quota looks fine.

marie: can you paste the pod event and node-affinity? quick grep from the autoscaler logs would help.

ajay: pasted below — truncated. looks like CA tried to scale a nodepool but GCE returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for GPUs in that zone.
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x5 over 5m)  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 9 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
Autoscaler: scale request -> nodepool-usw1-b-gpu: desired=4 current=2 -> API error: quotaExceeded: Insufficient GPUs in zone us-west1-b
```

ajay: also noticed a flurry of node deletions ~09:58 from preemptible churn which triggered rebalancing.

liam: probs preemptibles + scheduled maintenance + a short-lived regional retiering. We saw similar pattern last month but there fallback routed to other zones inside same region. Why didn't that happen here?

dana: looks like `topologySpreadConstraints` + `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` in the pod spec is pinning them to specific zones. some of our training jobs request `topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone` + `matchLabel` on nodepool. that prevents cross-zone placement unless CA creates nodes in that zone.

marie: we also have a nodeSelector that sets `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: p4d` on the pod. nodepool-usw1-c only has p3 equivalents, so CA won't provision incompatible types.

ajay: two threads of mitigation being discussed: 1) relax strict topology/instance-type constraints to allow cross-zone placement to other GPU families (with quantization/compatibility checks at runtime), 2) implement cross-cluster fallback to a warm pool in us-west2 that can accept workload with network path via VPC peer. both have tradeoffs.

liam: cross-cluster fallback cost: inter-region egress + cold cache on KV -> higher latency. Also private VPC peering currently limits throughput 1Gb between projects, needs network team signoff.

dana: ops-bot, can you pull peering link stats for redwood-prod-usw1 <-> redwood-prod-usw2 for the last 2 hours?

ops-bot: @dana pulled peering metrics: avg RTT 12ms, egress 150Mbps peak, no packet loss. Full report https://internal.monitoring/peers/usw1-usw2 (read-only).

marie: CA strategy change suggestion: add a short-lived override to allow `instance-type: flexible-gpu` label + toleration for noncritical training pods. This gives CA the option to spin up compatible nodes in other zones without manual nodepool changes. We could gate by priorityClass preemption.

ajay: config snippet idea for cluster-autoscaler (k8s CA configmap):
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--expander=least-waste
```
and on our nodegroup template add label `gpu-family-flex: "true"` for fallback nodes.

liam: need to exercise compatibility matrix for models — p4->p3 differences especially memory bandwidth. @marie can you run quick smoke tests with sample workloads on p3 fallback image?

marie: starting a canary run now in us-west2 with a 2-node warm pool (non-preemptible). Will share perf numbers in ~20m.

dana: long-term: should we consider a federated scheduler that can route to a dedicated infer cluster (same region or cross-region) for GPU shortages? That would require auth/telemetry plumbing but might be cleaner than relaxing constraints per pod.

ajay: agree that the federated approach is ideal. Short term we need a runbook update. Proposed immediate runbook steps:
1) When Insufficient GPUs in zone: check nodepool scaling errors and preemptible churn.
2) If quotaExceeded -> try scale to sibling zones in same region unless pod has strict instance-type label.
3) If sibling zones exhausted, check warm-pool in fallback region and open a manual approval with network and cost ack.
4) If manual approval granted, toggle `gpu-family-flex` on selected podsets and bump CA override to allow cross-zone node creation.

liam: I'll draft a concise runbook PR. keep the default automated behavior conservative — don't auto-evacuate into cross-region unless cost flag set.

marie: can we also add a zero-downtime shim that downloads model weights from GCS to fallback nodes ahead of time? pre-warm caches. That reduces cold-start latency.

ajay: good idea — add prefetch job to Redwood job-controller that watches warm pools.

autoscaler-bot: CA alert suppressed for us-west1-b quotaExceeded at 1965000405 after manual nodepool bump applied by ajay.

ajay: applied temporary nodepool increase + enabled `gpu-family-flex` on the pending job groups. pods started scheduling at 10:45 UTC.

dana: follow-ups: marie to post performance numbers, liam to open runbook PR, ajay to propose CA default flags for flexible fallbacks, ops to validate peering throughput for sustained cross-region fallback.

marie: perf summary: fallback on p3 warm pool added ~120ms median added latency and ~18% throughput drop on heavy batch workloads. model quality unchanged.

liam: created runbook PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge_requests/1234 — please review.

ajay: marking this thread for postmortem if we get recurring hits. For now, follow the runbook and let's avoid automatic cross-region by default. :white_check_mark:

marie: thanks — I'll file a small telemetry alert to detect repeated zone GPU exhaustion patterns.

ajay: closing the immediate incident, leaving these as action items. Thanks all. :rocket:
